content.comment_body: Hi, I'm using my [product_name] to control some electronics with a toggle switch circuit. The issue is that the relays (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4) activate too quickly and don't properly engage my circuit. How can I increase this activation time? The switches are currently set to pulse mode. Thank you, [user_name]
Hello, You could try inserting an off-delay timer between the output and whatever is triggering it. Regards,

Thanks, I tested that idea but discovered the issue isn’t there. My electronic circuit, connected to the output relays of the PLC, toggles ON when receiving a pulse and OFF with another pulse. It works reliably when connected to a physical pulse switch, but only functions correctly about half the time when controlled by the PLC. It seems the PLC relays generate an extra brief pulse that causes the circuit to turn off. Has anyone solved this? Thanks, [user_name]
Hello, I don't think there's a software fix for this; you may need to use a debounce circuit on the inputs. Regards,
Thanks, I constructed a debounce circuit with a 10k resistor and a 0.1μF capacitor at the output, and the problem is now resolved!

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced an issue where the relay outputs of the [product_name] operated too quickly to properly activate an external toggle circuit, causing unreliable switching. Suggestions included using timers and hardware debouncing, and the issue was ultimately resolved by implementing a hardware debounce circuit, highlighting that the device may not fully replicate mechanical switch signals for sensitive electronics.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expected the [product_name] pulse-mode outputs to consistently and reliably trigger typical electronic circuits, similar to a physical pulse switch, and not produce unintended additional pulses or glitches.
